pointers.sentence: `django.template` holds two systems that its own docstring calls independent (`django/template/__init__.py`).

Django ships `django/template/backends/django.py:DjangoTemplates`, for its own language; `django/template/backends/jinja2.py:Jinja2`, for Jinja2; and `django/template/backends/dummy.py:TemplateStrings`, which fills in plain text with the standard library's `string.Template`.

Django ships `django/template/backends/django.py:DjangoTemplates`, for its own language; `django/template/backends/jinja2.py:Jinja2`, for Jinja2; and `django/template/backends/dummy.py:TemplateStrings`, which fills in plain text with the standard library's `string.Template`.

The functions of `django/template/loader.py` (`get_template`, `select_template`, `render_to_string`) ask each backend in turn for a template by name, and whatever template comes back is rendered by a method that takes a plain dictionary and, optionally, the request (`django/template/utils.py:EngineHandler`, `django/template/loader.py:get_template`).

A `DjangoTemplates` backend makes one `Engine` from its entry of `TEMPLATES`, asks it for every template it is asked for, and wraps each compiled template it returns in a small object that adapts the language's `Template.render`, which takes a `Context`, to the engine layer's, which takes a dictionary (`django/template/backends/django.py:DjangoTemplates.__init__`, `django/template/engine.py:Engine`, `django/template/backends/django.py:Template`).

`Template` here is `django/template/base.py:Template`; the backend's wrapper of the same name is a different class.*

A template is compiled when its `Template` is made: the constructor calls `Template.compile_nodelist`, which runs a lexer and then a parser over the source (`django/template/base.py:Template.compile_nodelist`).

It splits the text with one regular expression that matches `{% … %}`, `{{ … }}` and `{# … #}`, and makes a **token** of each piece: a text token for what lies between tags, a variable token for `{{ … }}`, a block token for `{% … %}`, and a comment token for `{# … #}`, each holding its contents with the delimiters stripped (`django/template/base.py:Lexer.tokenize`, `django/template/base.py:Lexer.create_token`).

It splits the text with one regular expression that matches `{% … %}`, `{{ … }}` and `{# … #}`, and makes a **token** of each piece: a text token for what lies between tags, a variable token for `{{ … }}`, a block token for `{% … %}`, and a comment token for `{# … #}`, each holding its contents with the delimiters stripped (`django/template/base.py:Lexer.tokenize`, `django/template/base.py:Lexer.create_token`).
The **parser** turns the flat list into a tree (`django/template/base.py:Parser.parse`).

Other libraries, such as those in the templatetags package of an application, are known to the engine by name and reach a template's parser only through `{% load %}` (`django/template/engine.py:Engine.__init__`, `django/template/base.py:Parser.add_library`).

Other libraries, such as those in the templatetags package of an application, are known to the engine by name and reach a template's parser only through `{% load %}` (`django/template/engine.py:Engine.__init__`, `django/template/base.py:Parser.add_library`).
`Engine.get_template` asks the engine's loaders for the name, in order, and the first that finds it wins (`django/template/engine.py:Engine.find_template`).
The source is read and the `Template` made, and so compiled, as soon as the name is found (`django/template/loaders/base.py:Loader.get_template`).

The cached loader keeps the compiled template under a key made from its name, and the next request for that name gets the same object without reading or parsing anything (`django/template/loaders/cached.py:Loader.get_template`).

It makes a `Context` with the dictionary on top, or, when there is a request, a `RequestContext`, and calls the compiled template's `render` (`django/template/backends/django.py:Template.render`, `django/template/context.py:make_context`).

It makes a `Context` with the dictionary on top, or, when there is a request, a `RequestContext`, and calls the compiled template's `render` (`django/template/backends/django.py:Template.render`, `django/template/context.py:make_context`).

A `RequestContext` also runs the engine's **context processors**, functions of the request that each return a dictionary of names (the CSRF token, the user, the request itself), when the template starts to render, and puts their names below the view's (`django/template/context.py:BaseContext`, `django/template/context.py:RequestContext.bind_template`).

`Template.render` then renders its `NodeList`: each node renders itself to a string, and the strings are joined (`django/template/base.py:Template.render`, `django/template/base.py:NodeList.render`).
`Template.render` then renders its `NodeList`: each node renders itself to a string, and the strings are joined (`django/template/base.py:Template.render`, `django/template/base.py:NodeList.render`).

A `VariableNode` asks its `FilterExpression` for a value, which looks the variable up in the context (each part of its dotted name tried as a key, then as an attribute, then as a number used as an index, and what it finds called if it can be called, unless it is marked not to be) and passes it through the filters; it then turns the value into a string, localised, and escaped for HTML unless the context has autoescaping off or the value is already marked safe (`django/template/base.py:VariableNode.render`, `django/template/base.py:render_value_in_context`).

A `VariableNode` asks its `FilterExpression` for a value, which looks the variable up in the context (each part of its dotted name tried as a key, then as an attribute, then as a number used as an index, and what it finds called if it can be called, unless it is marked not to be) and passes it through the filters; it then turns the value into a string, localised, and escaped for HTML unless the context has autoescaping off or the value is already marked safe (`django/template/base.py:VariableNode.render`, `django/template/base.py:render_value_in_context`).

What the nodes need to remember while one template renders, such as the position of a `{% cycle %}` or the blocks of an inheritance chain, they ordinarily keep in the context's `render_context` ([Rendering: nodes and the render context](templates/rendering.md)), a second stack that `Template.render` pushes as it starts and pops as it ends, so that each template rendered through it starts with an empty level of its own (`django/template/context.py:RenderContext`).

Inheritance itself is a matter of rendering: in a template that begins with `{% extends %}`, everything after the tag is parsed into one `ExtendsNode`, which at render time finds the parent template and renders the parent's tree in its place, with the child's blocks put where the parent's stand ([Inheritance and inclusion: `{% extends %}`, `{% block %}` and `{% include %}`](templates/inheritance.md)) (`django/template/loader_tags.py:ExtendsNode.render`).
